before.title: Primary FSGS with APOL1 branch
before.diseaseDescription: Bounded circulating-factor/immune primary FSGS and separate APOL1-associated kidney injury branch; excludes other genetic, adaptive, viral and drug-associated FSGS. APOL1-associated disease is not classified as idiopathic primary FSGS. Selected mechanistic and intervention reports; not comprehensive literature or treatment coverage.
before.releaseNote: Separate study-context views for primary FSGS serum activity, human anti-nephrin findings, experimental immune injury, APOL1 ion transport, transgenic injury, inaxaplin trial and DUPLEX. No universal causal circuit or comprehensive therapy catalogue. Source checks are agent abstract inspections; independent scientific review pending.

APOL1-associated disease is not classified as idiopathic primary FSGS. Selected mechanistic and intervention reports; not comprehensive literature or treatment coverage.

after.text: In the United States, sparsentan is approved to reduce proteinuria in patients aged eight years and older with FSGS without nephrotic syndrome.
limitations: Label restriction excludes nephrotic syndrome; no extrapolation to nephrotic primary FSGS.

after.text: Inaxaplin inhibited APOL1 channel function in preclinical cell assays.
limitations: Abstract-level inspection; no independent domain review or complete methods appraisal.

after.text: In a single-group phase 2a study, 13 adherent participants with two APOL1 risk variants and biopsy-proven FSGS had a mean 47.6% proteinuria reduction at 13 weeks.
limitations: Uncontrolled small short-term trial; no randomized effect estimate, established kidney-survival benefit or approval inference.

after.text: Despite greater proteinuria reduction, DUPLEX found no significant between-group eGFR-slope difference at 108 weeks.
limitations: Surrogate improvement must not be described as demonstrated overall trial kidney-function preservation.

after.text: DUPLEX showed greater partial proteinuria remission with sparsentan than irbesartan at 36 weeks (42% versus 26%).
limitations: Mixed FSGS eligibility; not proof of immunologic mechanism or applicability of current indication to nephrotic primary FSGS.

after.summary: US FDA indication for reducing proteinuria in FSGS without nephrotic syndrome, age eight years and older.
after.location: FDA announcement opening paragraph; mechanism in following paragraph

after.name: Inaxaplin (VX-147)
after.mechanismOfAction: Inhibits APOL1 channel function in preclinical assays.
after.indication: Investigational APOL1-associated proteinuric kidney disease; initial trial required two APOL1 risk variants and biopsy-proven FSGS.
after.trialPhase: Inspected efficacy report: phase 2a (NCT04340362); subsequent development not systematically curated
limitations: Small uncontrolled 13-week study; no randomized kidney-outcome efficacy established.
2026 sponsor updates identified in search; newer trial results not independently inspected or mapped.

after.name: Sparsentan (Filspari)
after.modality: Oral dual endothelin / angiotensin II receptor antagonist
after.mechanismOfAction: Dual endothelin and angiotensin II receptor antagonism, as described by FDA; specific receptor nodes not expanded in this map.
after.indication: US: reduce proteinuria in patients aged eight years and older with FSGS without nephrotic syndrome.
limitations: US label excludes nephrotic syndrome; not an approved treatment for the nephrotic primary-FSGS branch.
DUPLEX overall eGFR-slope endpoint was not significant despite proteinuria improvement.
FDA announcement notes hepatotoxicity/REMS; full prescribing information not appraised.

after.label: US sparsentan indication: FSGS without nephrotic syndrome, age 8+
